mechanism: VEGFxPD-L1 bispecific mAb-Trap/fusion protein designed to inhibit angiogenesis, block PD-L1/PD-1 signaling, and activate Fc-mediated ADCC/ADCP.
development_status: China Phase II first-line NSCLC chemotherapy-combination study is active by company report, although the ClinicalTrials.gov record remains not yet recruiting; global ex-Greater China rights reverted to ImmuneOnco after Axion/Instil termination in January 2026.
clinical_summary: NCT06746870 is a single-arm, open-label Phase II study of IMM2510 plus histology-based platinum doublet chemotherapy in first-line stage IV metastatic or recurrent NSCLC, with cohorts for non-squamous and squamous disease. The company reported the first NSCLC patient was dosed in December 2024 and, among 21 efficacy-evaluable first-line NSCLC patients at 10 mg/kg as of July 1, 2025, ORR was 61.9% overall and 80.0% in squamous NSCLC. Monotherapy data in previously treated squamous NSCLC showed ORR 35.3%, DCR 76.5%, and median PFS 9.4 months in 17 patients.
safety_summary: ClinicalTrials.gov lists safety, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary efficacy endpoints and excludes patients with prior PD-1/PD-L1 or VEGF therapy, uncontrolled bleeding risk, pulmonary fibrosis/severe pulmonary impairment, uncontrolled chronic disease, active infection, and uncontrolled brain metastases. Company interim reporting states no new safety signals were observed with the NSCLC chemo-combination and that monotherapy was well tolerated; immature company data and no posted trial results limit confidence.
management_tools: Biomarker criteria for EGFR, ALK, ROS1, PD-L1, and histology
evidence_gaps: No randomized Phase III data or registrational filing identified for NSCLC.
ClinicalTrials.gov status appears stale versus company-reported first patient dosing and enrollment.
Company-reported efficacy comes from small, early, open-label cohorts without a control arm.
No direct US or China launch timing found after January 2026 global-rights reversion.
No direct price exists; annual cost range uses US medical-benefit analogs.

expected_launch_window.method: Earliest plausible launch inferred from current Phase II status, no identified pivotal trial or filing, estimated study completion in 2026, and January 2026 global-rights reversion.
expected_launch_window.explanation: The asset remains early for first-line NSCLC and has no confirmed registrational program; partner termination adds strategic uncertainty, so launch timing should be treated as post-2030 and uncertain.

annual_cost_range.method: Used US analog biologic medical-benefit costs: low equals atezolizumab 1200 mg Q3W at $93.997 per 10 mg for 52/3 doses/year; high adds bevacizumab 15 mg/kg Q3W for a 70 kg patient at $74.355 per 10 mg. Chemotherapy costs excluded.
annual_cost_range.explanation: IMM2510 has no direct price. Atezolizumab anchors the PD-L1 component and atezolizumab plus bevacizumab anchors a combined PD-L1/VEGF biologic ceiling relevant to first-line NSCLC.

clinical_differentiation.method: Assessed mechanism novelty and early response signals against evidence maturity.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: Dual VEGF/PD-L1 blockade, VEGF-trap structure, and Fc effector design are differentiated, and early single-arm ORR is encouraging; lack of randomized data prevents a High rating.

budget_impact.method: Combined large first-line NSCLC eligible population with analog annual biologic cost range above $195,000 before chemotherapy.
budget_impact.explanation: A successful first-line NSCLC launch would enter a high-volume oncology category with high per-patient medical-benefit drug cost.

disruption_risk.method: Balanced potential class disruption from dual PD-L1/VEGF activity against early-stage evidence, China-only active data, and partner-rights disruption.
disruption_risk.explanation: IMM2510 could alter first-line NSCLC sequencing if randomized outcomes confirm the early response signal, but current evidence and commercial pathway remain immature.

recommended_action.method: Action level based on pre-pivotal status, immature evidence, and lack of direct launch timing.
recommended_action.explanation: Track updated NSCLC data, pivotal-trial decisions, global partnership status, and registry updates; active planning is premature before registrational evidence emerges.

quality_flags: ClinicalTrials.gov record is not yet recruiting and last updated in December 2024, while company reporting says first NSCLC patient was dosed in December 2024 and 33 first-line NSCLC patients were enrolled by July 2025.
Global ex-Greater China development rights reverted to ImmuneOnco in January 2026 after Axion/Instil termination, creating uncertainty for US development and launch assumptions.
No direct price is available; annual cost uses atezolizumab and bevacizumab analogs and excludes chemotherapy administration and supportive-care costs.
Efficacy and safety summaries rely partly on company-reported early open-label data with no posted ClinicalTrials.gov results.
